title: Persistent post-parse completion tracking (replaces dart-import fast-path gate, fixes interrupted-parse poisoning)
description:
Two bugs, one mechanism.

Bug 1: the NoChanges fast path (src/pipeline.rs:436-443) is gated on !db.has_unresolved_dart_imports() (src/db/mod.rs:1355), which only excludes dart:% — external pub package: imports (215 in swe_dashboard) never resolve, so the gate is permanently open and the full post-parse pipeline (~8s, HRR-dominated) runs on EVERY no-change parse of any real Dart project. Rust equivalent: 16ms.

Bug 2: an interrupted parse (Ctrl-C, crash, cancel) leaves files committed with current content_hash but refs unresolved and derived data missing (observed on redox-kernel: 160/52,718 refs resolved, zero pagerank/HRR/components/health). Next parse sees no changed files + a prior snapshot → fast path → never repairs. Ref resolution only covers dirty files, so even changed-file parses never heal the orphans. Only fix today is deleting the DB. Note record_snapshot also runs on the Err/cancel path, so has_previous_snapshot is not a completion signal.

Fix (design from 2026-06-10 perf review):
1. Per-file work flag: files.needs_resolution, set inside replace_file_data's transaction, cleared inside resolve_file_refs' write transaction. The resolution work-queue lives in the DB, atomically consistent with the data it describes. post_parse resolves WHERE needs_resolution=1, not an in-memory set.
2. Global completion marker: single-row index_meta table with data_generation (bumped whenever any file row changes) and derived_complete_generation (written only after post_parse_sequence + snapshot fully commit). Fast path: skip post-parse iff zero files parsed/deleted/pruned AND no needs_resolution rows AND generations match. Delete has_unresolved_dart_imports gate entirely.
Interruption at any point then self-heals on the next parse, incremental or full.

acceptance_criteria.text: No-change parse of swe_dashboard takes <100ms (fast path fires despite external package: imports)
Kill -9 a parse mid-resolution; next no-change parse detects incomplete state and completes resolution + derived data
needs_resolution flag set/cleared transactionally with the data it describes

execution_record:
Implemented per-file `needs_resolution` flag + global `index_meta` generation pair. Key changes:

- Migration 0037: adds `needs_resolution` column to `files`, creates `index_meta` table with generation pair
- `replace_file_data`: sets `needs_resolution=1` and bumps `data_generation` atomically
- `delete_file_cascade`: bumps `data_generation` atomically
- New `replace_refs_and_clear_resolution`: wraps ref writes + needs_resolution clear in a single transaction
- `post_parse_sequence`: queries dirty files from DB instead of in-memory HashSet; marks deleted-symbol back-references durably
- Fast path: replaced `has_previous_snapshot + has_unresolved_dart_imports` with `has_pending_work` (checks needs_resolution + generation match)
- Completion marker: `set_derived_complete` called only after successful post_parse + snapshot
- Reindex resets generations to 0

All 723 tests pass. Acceptance criteria 3-4 (gate removal, transactional flag) verified structurally. Criteria 1-2 (perf, crash recovery) need integration testing against a real Dart workspace."

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: **needs-attention**

**Finding 1 [high]: Dependent-file re-resolution not transactionally covered**
`post_parse_sequence` calls `mark_needs_resolution` for back-references AFTER `replace_file_data`/`delete_file_cascade` has already committed. Those paths delete old symbols with FK cascades wiping `refs.target_symbol_id`, so `find_files_referencing_symbols` can find nothing. A kill between committed file mutation and the post-parse mark leaves no durable queue entry for dependent files — next parse sees generation mismatch but has no `deleted_symbol_ids` and no `needs_resolution` rows for those dependents.

Recommendation: Move dependent-file discovery and `needs_resolution=1` into the same transaction that removes/replaces old symbols, before cascading deletes erase the evidence.

**Finding 2 [medium]: Migration initializes existing indexes as complete by default**
Migration 0037 adds `needs_resolution DEFAULT 0` and `index_meta` with `data_generation=0, derived_complete_generation=0`. For an existing DB with a previously interrupted/poisoned index, `has_pending_work` returns false — the fast path fires and stale derived data survives.

Recommendation: On migration, mark existing file rows `needs_resolution=1` or initialize generations as mismatched so the first post-upgrade parse forces full recovery.
